reran: cmd.sh on w4-int, w3-base and 2.13.18: identical (NullPointerException from CAS_ROOT for snapshot() and readOnlySnapshot()). Also 2.12.20: same NPE. My variant on w4-int and 2.13.18: on a read-only snapshot cast to TrieMap, iterator, size, isEmpty, keySet, values, view, toMap, clone, equals, hashCode, map, filter, ++, get and serialization all work; clear() throws the same NPE; put, update, remove, getOrElseUpdate, ++=, filterInPlace and mapValuesInPlace never return (jstack: spinning at 100% CPU in INode.GCAS_Complete via rec_insertif, because GCAS always aborts when the map is read-only and the insert retries forever); also on 2.13.18.
user_impact: Only code that holds a read-only snapshot as a TrieMap or mutable.Map: readOnlySnapshot() is typed collection.Map, so it takes a cast or a type test such as `case m: mutable.Map[K, V] => m ++= more`, or a helper that takes a TrieMap and snapshots or updates its argument. Rare, but the result is an unexplained NullPointerException or, for any mutator, a thread that spins forever.
fixability: clear cut: readOnlySnapshot() returns this when isReadOnly; snapshot() returns new TrieMap(r.copyToGen(new Gen, this), <a fresh updater>, hashing, equality) without the RDCSS when isReadOnly; mutators throw UnsupportedOperationException when isReadOnly (as Collections.unmodifiableMap does), which the Scaladoc's 'cannot be modified' already promises. No binary cost.
regression: no (the read-only path dates from the 2012 TrieMap import, 2.10; 2.12.20 is the same)
links: retronym/scala PR 677 (clone and TrieMap.from as snapshots) guards its new calls with nonReadOnly because of exactly this and could take the fix, or the fix can go first and the guards be dropped. Wave-three KT2, KT6 and wave-one M9 are other TrieMap causes. No library method calls snapshot() or readOnlySnapshot() on a read-only receiver: iterator, values, keySet, view, size and isEmpty test nonReadOnly first.
note: Understated: the hunter tested reads and the two snapshot methods but not mutators. On a read-only snapshot every mutator except clear() livelocks; that is the worse half of the same root cause (the read-only state is handled only on the read paths) and should be in the finding and the fix. Expected behaviour: the readOnlySnapshot Scaladoc says the snapshot 'cannot be modified', not that snapshotting it fails; java.util.concurrent has no snapshot analogue, and the nearest Java read-only views (Collections.unmodifiableMap, Map.copyOf, which returns its argument when already immutable) answer every read and throw UnsupportedOperationException from mutators. No scala/bug report found (TrieMap issue list read) and nothing in the branch index.
